My name is on this land only for one season since I rent it, so I must be careful not to spend too much. Cassava and yam do well here in the South East with our good rains, but the soil is tired and I know yam especially needs good nutrients to give big tubers. I will buy a little NPK 15-15-15 if I can get it from the agro-dealer, and I will carry goat droppings and household compost to the mounds. I plant my own yam setts and cassava cuttings from last year — improved cassava from the extension people would be good but I cannot find them easily, so I stay with what I know. My wife and older children will help me with the mounding and weeding, but clearing and making the heaps is heavy work so I must hire some young men for a few days.
